section: Cultural and Educational Rights - Articles 29-30; the right to property and the 44th Amendment
subsections: Right to property - Article 31 journey, deleting amendment, Article 300A
Article 30 - minority educational institutions, compensation clause
Article 29 - interests of minorities, language, script, culture, admission

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the position of the Right to Property under the Constitution as it stood in 1950?
o: It was guaranteed only under Article 31 as a legal right
It was a DPSP under Article 39
It was a statutory right under the Representation of the People Act, 1951
It was a Fundamental Right under Articles 19(1)(f) and 31
accepted.x: In 1950, the Right to Property was a Fundamental Right under Article 19(1)(f), relating to acquiring, holding and disposing of property, and Article 31, relating to deprivation and acquisition of property.
accepted.tq: Use the historical position of the right rather than its present constitutional status.
accepted.sec: Right to property - Article 31 journey, deleting amendment, Article 300A

accepted.s: The 1st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1951 inserted which of the following provisions to protect land reform laws?
o: Articles 39A and 43B and the Eleventh Schedule
Articles 31A and 31B and the Ninth Schedule
Articles 32A and 33 and the Eighth Schedule
Articles 30(1A) and 300A and the Tenth Schedule
accepted.x: The 1st Amendment inserted Articles 31A and 31B and created the Ninth Schedule to provide protection to land reform laws.
accepted.tq: Match the amendment with the constitutional provisions introduced by it.
accepted.sec: Right to property - Article 31 journey, deleting amendment, Article 300A

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding constitutional amendments affecting the Right to Property:
1. The 4th Amendment was enacted in 1955.
2. The 17th Amendment was enacted in 1964.
3. The 25th Amendment was enacted in 1971.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: All three statements are correct: the 4th, 17th and 25th Amendments were enacted in 1955, 1964 and 1971 respectively, and each affected the constitutional treatment of property and compensation.
accepted.tq: Check each year independently before selecting the coded combination.
accepted.sec: Right to property - Article 31 journey, deleting amendment, Article 300A

accepted.s: With reference to the 17th Amendment relating to property, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: It inserted Article 300A in Part XII
It made all land acquisition free from judicial review
It provided that land under personal cultivation could be acquired only on payment of market value
It abolished Article 31 altogether
accepted.x: The 17th Amendment provided that land under personal cultivation could be acquired only on payment of market value.
accepted.tq: Identify the amendment-specific detail instead of choosing the broader property-right changes.
accepted.sec: Right to property - Article 31 journey, deleting amendment, Article 300A

accepted.s: The 44th Amendment Act, 1978 brought about which one of the following changes?
o: It shifted Article 21A from Part IV to Part III
It inserted Articles 31A and 31B in Part III
It converted the Right to Property into a Fundamental Right available only to citizens
It deleted Articles 19(1)(f) and 31 from Part III and placed the Right to Property under Article 300A
accepted.x: The 44th Amendment deleted Article 19(1)(f) and Article 31 from Part III and made property a constitutional legal right under Article 300A in Part XII, Chapter IV.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the deleting amendment from the earlier amendments that protected land reforms.
accepted.sec: Right to property - Article 31 journey, deleting amendment, Article 300A

accepted.s: Article 300A provides that—
o: No citizen shall be deprived of property except by executive order
No company shall be deprived of property under any circumstances
No person shall be deprived of property except with the consent of Parliament
No person shall be deprived of property save by authority of law
accepted.x: Article 300A states that no person shall be deprived of his property save by authority of law.
accepted.tq: Recall the exact constitutional wording and avoid replacing 'authority of law' with executive action.
accepted.sec: Right to property - Article 31 journey, deleting amendment, Article 300A

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly explains the present constitutional status of the Right to Property?
o: It is a constitutional legal right under Article 300A, available to all persons
It is a constitutional legal right enforceable against legislation under Article 32
It is only a statutory right available to citizens under the RPA, 1951
It is a Fundamental Right enforceable under Article 32
accepted.x: The Right to Property is a constitutional legal right under Article 300A. It is available to all persons, including citizens, non-citizens and companies, but is not a Fundamental Right enforceable under Article 32.
accepted.tq: Separate Fundamental Rights from constitutional legal rights by status, beneficiaries and remedy.
accepted.sec: Right to property - Article 31 journey, deleting amendment, Article 300A

accepted.s: A person is dispossessed of property by an executive order without any authority of law. Which constitutional provision is most directly attracted?
o: Article 300A
Article 31 as a continuing Fundamental Right
Article 19(1)(f)
Article 301
accepted.x: Article 300A protects against deprivation of property without authority of law and operates against executive action. Article 301 and the deleted Articles 31 and 19(1)(f) do not provide the applicable present remedy.
accepted.tq: Ask which constitutional provision governs the action of the authority actually dispossessing the person.
accepted.sec: Right to property - Article 31 journey, deleting amendment, Article 300A

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding enforcement of Article 300A is correct?
o: It can be enforced only by filing a petition before the Election Commission
It cannot be enforced through any judicial proceeding
It can be enforced only through Article 32
It can be enforced through Article 226 or an ordinary civil suit, but not through Article 32 as a Fundamental Right
accepted.x: Since Article 300A does not confer a Fundamental Right, a claim may be pursued under Article 226 or through an ordinary suit, rather than as an Article 32 Fundamental Rights petition.
accepted.tq: Use the remedy-based distinction between Fundamental Rights and other constitutional rights.
accepted.sec: Right to property - Article 31 journey, deleting amendment, Article 300A

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements regarding the Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 is correct?
1. Social Impact Assessment is mandatory.
2. Consent of 70 per cent is required for public-private partnership projects.
3. Consent of 80 per cent is required for private projects.
4. Unused acquired land is to be returned after five years.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
o: 1, 2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 4 only
2, 3 and 4 only
accepted.x: The 2013 Act replaced the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, and provides for mandatory Social Impact Assessment, 70 per cent consent for PPP projects, 80 per cent for private projects and return of unused land after five years.
accepted.tq: Separate the consent percentages and test all numerical conditions individually.
accepted.sec: Right to property - Article 31 journey, deleting amendment, Article 300A

accepted.s: Under the Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013, the maximum compensation mentioned for rural and urban areas respectively is—
o: Twice the market value in both areas
Four times the market value in both areas
Four times the market value and twice the market value
Twice the market value and four times the market value
accepted.x: The compensation may be up to four times the market value in rural areas and twice the market value in urban areas.
accepted.tq: Read the comparison in the stated order: rural first and urban second.
accepted.sec: Right to property - Article 31 journey, deleting amendment, Article 300A

accepted.s: Article 30(1A), inserted by the 44th Amendment, deals primarily with—
o: Exemption of minority institutions from all State regulation
Compulsory acquisition of property of minority educational institutions
Appointment of teachers in minority institutions
Reservation of seats in minority institutions
accepted.x: Article 30(1A) concerns compulsory acquisition of the property of a minority educational institution. The amount fixed must not restrict or abrogate the right guaranteed by Article 30.
accepted.tq: Link the sub-clause number with its specific subject instead of the general right under Article 30(1).
accepted.sec: Article 30 - minority educational institutions, compensation clause

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about Article 30:
1. The State shall not discriminate against minority institutions in granting aid.
2. The right to administer a minority institution is completely immune from State regulation.
3. The State may regulate standards of education without destroying the minority character of the institution.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. The right under Article 30 is not absolute; the State may regulate educational standards, but it cannot destroy the minority character of the institution.
accepted.tq: Reject the absolute statement while retaining the distinction between regulation of standards and destruction of minority character.
accepted.sec: Article 30 - minority educational institutions, compensation clause

accepted.s: The 25 per cent quota under the Right to Education Act does not apply to minority schools in view of the decision in—
o: St. Stephen's College v. University of Delhi
T.M.A. Pai Foundation v. State of Karnataka
Pramati Educational and Cultural Trust v. Union of India
P.A. Inamdar v. State of Maharashtra
accepted.x: In Pramati, decided in 2014, the Supreme Court held that the RTE Act's 25 per cent quota does not apply to minority schools.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the case concerning RTE exemption from cases concerning autonomy, preference or reservation.
accepted.sec: Article 30 - minority educational institutions, compensation clause

accepted.s: According to the cited NCPCR figure, disadvantaged enrolment in minority schools was approximately—
o: 5.87 per cent
8.76 per cent
12.50 per cent
25 per cent
accepted.x: The cited NCPCR figure is 8.76 per cent disadvantaged enrolment in minority schools.
accepted.tq: Identify the precise percentage rather than confusing it with the RTE quota figure of 25 per cent.
accepted.sec: Article 30 - minority educational institutions, compensation clause

accepted.s: Article 29(1) protects the right of—
o: All persons, including non-citizens, to preserve any cultural practice
Only religious minorities to conserve their religion
Any section of citizens having a distinct language, script or culture to conserve the same
Only linguistic minorities to establish educational institutions
accepted.x: Article 29(1) grants any section of citizens having a distinct language, script or culture the right to conserve it. Its wording is wider than the term 'minorities'.
accepted.tq: Focus on the wider phrase 'any section of citizens' instead of narrowing it to minorities.
accepted.sec: Article 29 - interests of minorities, language, script, culture, admission

accepted.s: Which one of the following grounds is NOT expressly included in Article 29(2) as a basis for denying admission to a State-maintained or State-aided educational institution?
o: Race
Place of birth
Religion
Language
accepted.x: Article 29(2) prohibits denial of admission on grounds only of religion, race, caste or language. Sex and place of birth are not included in this list.
accepted.tq: Find the omitted ground rather than selecting one of the four expressly listed grounds.
accepted.sec: Article 29 - interests of minorities, language, script, culture, admission

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Article 29:
1. Article 29(1) is available to any section of citizens with a distinct language, script or culture.
2. Article 29(2) protects admission to State-maintained or State-aided institutions.
3. The protection under Article 29 is available to non-citizens also.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Article 29 is available only to citizens, so statement 3 is false.
accepted.tq: Test both the substantive protection and the class of persons entitled to it.
accepted.sec: Article 29 - interests of minorities, language, script, culture, admission

accepted.s: A political promise to conserve the language of a particular section of citizens is, by itself, treated under the Representation of the People Act, 1951 as—
o: A violation of Article 30(2)
Not a corrupt practice
An electoral offence in every case
A corrupt practice
accepted.x: A political promise to conserve a section's language is not treated as a corrupt practice under the Representation of the People Act, 1951.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a cultural or linguistic promise from a legally defined corrupt electoral practice.
accepted.sec: Article 29 - interests of minorities, language, script, culture, admission

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly matches the right with its constitutional position?
o: Right to Vote — Article 326 and statutory provisions under the Representation of the People Acts
Right to Work — Article 21A
Right to Information — Article 41 only
Education for children aged 6–14 — Article 45 alone
accepted.x: Voting is based on adult suffrage under Article 326 and statutory provisions including Sections 62 of the RPA, 1951 and 19 of the RPA, 1950. The other options misstate the constitutional sources of work, information and education.
accepted.tq: Trace each right to its precise Article and statutory mechanism rather than relying on its general name.
accepted.sec: Fundamental vs constitutional/legal right - classification

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below:
List-I (Case)
A. In re Kerala Education Bill
B. St. Stephen's College v. University of Delhi
C. T.M.A. Pai Foundation v. State of Karnataka
D. P.A. Inamdar v. State of Maharashtra

List-II (Holding)
1. State is the unit for determining a linguistic or religious minority
2. Aided minority college may prefer its own community up to 50 per cent of seats
3. State cannot impose reservation on unaided minority or non-minority professional institutions
4. State may regulate standards without destroying minority character

Select the correct answer.
accepted.x: In re Kerala Education Bill corresponds to regulation of standards; St. Stephen's permits preference up to 50 per cent; T.M.A. Pai identifies the State as the unit; and P.A. Inamdar rejects such State-imposed reservation in the stated institutions.
accepted.tq: Start from the distinctive case holdings and then verify the remaining pairs.
accepted.sec: Minority institution cases

accepted.s: In St. Stephen's College v. University of Delhi, the Supreme Court held that an aided minority college may prefer candidates from its own community up to—
o: 33 per cent of the seats
25 per cent of the seats
75 per cent of the seats
50 per cent of the seats
accepted.x: The decision recognised that an aided minority college may prefer candidates from its own community up to 50 per cent of the seats.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the case-specific percentage from the separate 25 per cent RTE quota figure.
accepted.sec: Minority institution cases

accepted.s: The decision in P.A. Inamdar v. State of Maharashtra is associated with which proposition?
o: The State cannot impose reservation on unaided minority or non-minority professional institutions
The RTE 25 per cent quota applies to all minority schools
The State may impose reservation on unaided minority professional institutions
Minority rights under Article 30 are entirely absolute
accepted.x: P.A. Inamdar held that the State cannot impose reservation on unaided minority or non-minority professional institutions in the manner stated.
accepted.tq: Identify the case by its specific reservation holding and reject absolute formulations.
accepted.sec: Minority institution cases
